annotations.description: Keeping a hand with 4 Islands and 0 red sources in a UR deck. While the hand can cast its colorless artifacts and Perilous Voyage, it has no red mana to cast red creatures like Tectonic Giant, Onakke Ogre, or Dragon Hatchling. The hand lacks early pressure and relies on drawing red sources naturally.
annotations.actionTaken: Kept the 7-card hand with no red mana sources
annotations.betterLine: Mulligan to 6 looking for a hand with both colors of mana. A 6-card hand with at least one red source and reasonable spells would likely perform better than a 7-card hand missing an entire color.

annotations.description: With 3 Islands already in hand and only 3-mana spells to cast, GPT5 Spike kept one Island on top during scry instead of bottoming both. They already have enough lands to cast all their spells (Bloodline Pretender, Heirloom Blade at 3 mana, Faerie Seer at 1), so drawing another Island is low value compared to finding action/threats.
annotations.actionTaken: Bottomed only one Island, keeping the other on top of library
annotations.betterLine: Bottom both Islands to dig toward spells, since hand already has 3 Islands which is sufficient to cast everything available

annotations.description: Cast Bloodrage Brawler before playing a land drop. Playing a Mountain first is free and gets them to 3 lands on board, which is strictly better. With Tectonic Giant at 4 mana and Terror of the Peaks at 5 mana in hand, getting lands on board as quickly as possible is important.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Bloodrage Brawler with only 2 Mountains on board, before using the available land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play a Mountain first (going to 3 lands on board), then cast Bloodrage Brawler. This costs nothing and leaves you one turn closer to casting Tectonic Giant and Terror of the Peaks.

annotations.description: Cast Onakke Ogre (vanilla 4/2) instead of Tectonic Giant (3/4 with powerful attack trigger dealing 3 damage or generating card advantage). With exactly 4 Mountains untapped, Tectonic Giant was castable and is dramatically more powerful. Getting Tectonic Giant down a turn earlier means an extra attack trigger worth 3 damage or a card, and it has a much better body (3/4 vs 4/2) against the opponent's blue deck that likely has bounce/removal.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Tectonic Giant for 4 mana - it's one of the best Limited cards available, applies massive pressure with its attack trigger, and has a superior body. Next turn, play a 5th Mountain and cast Terror of the Peaks for an even more devastating follow-up.

annotations.description: Rapacious Dragon is the weakest of the three options to deploy first. Terror of the Peaks is a 5/4 flyer that punishes targeted removal (costs 3 life) and would trigger off future creatures like Rapacious Dragon for additional damage. Tectonic Giant also applies more pressure. Rapacious Dragon's Treasures enable future plays, but the sequencing is worse - deploying Terror first maximizes its trigger value when Rapacious Dragon comes down next turn (dealing 3 damage from Terror's ability).
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Rapacious Dragon, getting a 3/3 flyer and 2 Treasures
annotations.betterLine: Cast Terror of the Peaks first as the 5/4 flyer that taxes removal and synergizes with future creature plays. Next turn, casting Rapacious Dragon would trigger Terror for 3 damage to any target while also providing Treasures.

annotations.description: GPT5 Spike declined to attack with Faerie Seer (4/2 with Heirloom Blade) when all of the opponent's creatures were tapped or had summoning sickness. This was a completely free 4 damage with zero risk of being blocked. At 8 life facing potential lethal next turn, every point of damage matters.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Faerie Seer for 4 free damage, bringing the opponent from 19 to 15 life.

annotations.description: At opponent's 1 life, Terror of the Peaks is significantly better than Tectonic Giant. Terror of the Peaks has flying (harder to block), its 'costs 3 life to target' ability makes it literally untargetable by opponent spells at 1 life, and its ETB trigger on future creatures could deal lethal damage immediately. Tectonic Giant can be bounced or removed by the opponent's spells.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Tectonic Giant instead of Terror of the Peaks
annotations.betterLine: Cast Terror of the Peaks. At 1 life, the opponent cannot target it with spells (costs 3 additional life), it has flying to avoid blockers, and any future creature ETB deals lethal damage.
